articles.title: Haaland, la gran decisión
articles.standfirst: Una sanción al City podría hacer que el goleador noruego sacuda el mercado cambiando de aires
articles.summary: Una sanción al City podría hacer que el goleador noruego sacuda el mercado cambiando de aires
articles.body: El Caso Manchester City, tras destapar ayer The Athletic que el club ha sido declarado culpable en prácticamente todas las acusaciones (en 114 de 115) relacionadas con infracciones de las regulaciones financieras de la Premier League, puede tener consecuencias muy graves para la entidad. Y no sólo por la posible pérdida de puntos, el descenso o la retirada de títulos, sino por la fuga de estrellas. Y ahí entra en escena Erling Braut Haaland. El goleador noruego puede encontrarse ante una decisión que hoy parece remota, pero que el futuro del Manchester City podría convertir en inevitable. El delantero renovó hasta 2034, un contrato en ese momento de diez temporadas que parecía blindar su continuidad en el Etihad durante prácticamente toda la década y que representaba, además, una declaración de intenciones sobre su compromiso con el proyecto. Sin embargo, todo puede cambiar si la sanción que finalmente reciba el club tiene consecuencias deportivas de una dimensión extraordinaria. Porque no es lo mismo afrontar una multa o una deducción de puntos asumible que encontrarse con una sanción capaz de provocar el descenso del equipo, ya sea directamente o como consecuencia de una pérdida de puntos que haga inviable su permanencia en la Premier. Si se llega a ese extremo, el escenario cambiaría por completo y Haaland tendría que valorar qué hacer con su futuro pese a tener todavía contrato por muchos años. En el entorno del delantero siempre se ha manejado la posibilidad de que su contrato contemple mecanismos de salida para determinados escenarios, aunque no está confirmado que exista una cláusula específica que se active automáticamente en caso de descenso, y las informaciones sobre las condiciones exactas del vínculo no son coincidentes. Lo que sí parece evidente es que una situación tan extraordinaria como la pérdida de categoría modificaría sustancialmente las circunstancias bajo las que el ex del Dortmund decidió comprometerse tanto tiempo. El Real Madrid ya estuvo detrás del noruego antes de que éste eligiera Mánchester. El club blanco estudió su incorporación, mantuvo contactos durante aquel proceso y nunca ha dejado de considerarle como uno de los grandes delanteros de su generación. Por eso, si algún día el jugador quedara realmente en disposición de escuchar ofertas, el Bernabéu aparecería inmediatamente como uno de los destinos naturales para él. Sin embargo, con la realidad del Real Madrid a día de hoy, parece completamente utópico pensar en su llegada a Chamartín. Mbappé tiene contrato hasta 2029, Vinicius recién renovado hasta 2032... y Bellingham también hasta 2029, aunque el club blanco ya estaría valorando una mejora sustancial de contrato. Es decir, que para la llegada del nórdico debería salir, al menos, uno de los tres. Por su parte, el Barcelona tampoco vive alejado de Haaland, ni mucho menos. Deco ha tanteado en varias ocasiones la situación del delantero con Rafaela Pimenta y el club azulgrana conoce de primera mano cuál es el escenario alrededor del jugador. De hecho, a nivel público nunca se han mordido la lengua y han reconocido que el jugador interesa en el club azulgrana. Esto convierte al club presidido por Joan Laporta en un actor a tener muy en cuenta si algún día se abre esa ventana. La operación, evidentemente, exigiría una capacidad económica extraordinaria y una planificación financiera acorde con el coste de un jugador de este nivel, pero lo cierto es que todo encajaría para su llegada, más aún tras una confección de plantilla sin un delantero goleador 'clásico' después de la salida de Robert Lewandowski. Lo que resulta mucho menos probable, en caso de que Haaland termine rompiendo con el Manchester City por una crisis deportiva de esta magnitud, es que su siguiente destino sea otro gran club de la Premier. No parece que el escenario natural sea una salida del City para marcharse a otro rival directo en Inglaterra. Su relación con la entidad, todo lo que ha construido desde su llegada, la conexión de pasado con su familia y el significado de una eventual ruptura hacen que una operación así tenga una lectura muy diferente a un simple cambio de equipo. Por eso, el tamaño de la sanción será determinante. Si el castigo no altera de manera sustancial la capacidad competitiva del City, Haaland seguirá teniendo todos los motivos para continuar en Mánchester y cumplir el contrato que firmó hasta 2034. Pero si la resolución provoca algo mayor, uno de los mejores goleadores del último lustro podría agitar el mercado. Tiene 26 años, una media de 1,14 goles por encuentro y un valor de mercado de 220 millones de euros. Un valor seguro y diferencial que puede volar lejos del Etihad.

articles.title: El Spotify Camp Nou reluce: tras acoger la final de la Champions 2029, optimismo para la del Mundial 2030
articles.standfirst: El Barça y las instituciones creen en sus opciones pese a que todo apunta a que será en Casablanca
articles.summary: El Barça y las instituciones creen en sus opciones pese a que todo apunta a que será en Casablanca
articles.body: El Spotify Camp Nou está siendo una de las grandes alegrías del barcelonismo, no sólo porque el equipo de Flick gana todos los partidos que disputa ante su grada o porque es una de sus principales fuentes de ingresos, sino porque el remodelado estadio culé está siendo reconocido y coloca al club catalán en el panorama futbolístico internacional. Tras ser designado como el escenario que acogerá la final de la Champions League de 2029, hay optimismo en todos los estamentos para albergar la del Mundial de 2030. El Barcelona y las instituciones catalanas creen firmemente en las opciones de que el Spotify Camp Nou sea la sede del último partido de la competición que tendrá lugar dentro de cuatro años y que será organizada por tres países: España, Portugal y Marruecos. El club y los organismos llevan tiempo trabajando en los argumentos y el hecho de que el pasado día 15 el feudo azulgrana fuera designado para albergar la final de la Champions League 2029 les invita aún más a ser positivos. El gran rival, y favorito, es el estadio Hassan II de Casablanca. También opta el Santiago Bernabéu. “Es el mejor escenario para la final. No es que sea optimista, es que soy realista. Creo que el mejor escenario para la final del Mundial 2030 es el Spotify Camp Nou”, comentó en las últimas horas Berni Álvarez, conseller d’Esports de la Generalitat de Catalunya en el programa Tot Costa. “Hemos hecho hasta ahora el mejor trabajo, muy coordinado con el Ajuntament de Barcelona y el club, sin estridencias y seguramente sin lo que han hecho los otros”, añadió. El conseller de la Generalitat se mostró orgulloso de las gestiones realizadas, aunque dejó entrever que es una decisión que va más allá del proyecto presentado: "Tendremos oportunidades, será cuestión de estar en el momento adecuado en el sitio adecuado. Pero no dependerá al cien por cien de tu trabajo, y eso quizás no es justo, pero estoy muy contento de todos los pasos que estamos dando porque los estamos dando bien”. La FIFA está pendiente de anunciar la sede de la final, aunque recientemente Fouzi Lekjaa, presidente de la federación marroquí, aseguró que se celebraría en el estadio Hassan II de Casablanca, que aún está en construcción y cuya inauguración está prevista para finales de 2027. Tendrá 115.000 localidades y será el mayor del mundo por capacidad. Muchos le dan por favorito, incluido el alcalde de Madrid, José Luis Martínez Almeida. "No soy optimista de que la final sea en el Santiago Bernabéu porque considero que ellos quieren esa final y lógicamente están actuando a nivel político e institucional para lograr esa final", afirmó a principios de esta semana. Pero en las instituciones catalanas y en el Barça hay optimismo. "La final del Mundial no debería ser ni en Casablanca ni en Madrid, debería ser en el Spotify Camp Nou", sentenció Joan Laporta hace unos días en el programa Què t'hi jugues. "Lo digo por una razón. 105.000 espectadores. Yo creo que esto la FIFA lo tendrá en cuenta. Y además... ya se organizó una final del Mundial en el Santiago Bernabéu en 1982. Con todos los respetos a Marruecos, la final del Mundial 2030 se debería jugar en el estado español, y además España es una selección que campeona del mundo", indicó convencido el presidente del Barcelona.

articles.title: Nations League: Wes Burns says Craig Bellamy support was crucial during injury recovery
articles.summary: Winger Wes Burns hopes to repay Craig Bellamy's support during a long-term injury by making an impact for Wales in the Nations League.
articles.body:
It is usually the manager who pulls a player to one side before or after training to offer a word of advice or appreciation.

But it was the other way round with Craig Bellamy and Wes Burns.

Wales winger Burns says he made a point of pulling Bellamy aside to thank him for the "massive" support he gave him after a career-threatening knee injury that ended his Premier League dream in 2025.

Without Bellamy's backing, Burns said, his Wales career might have gone the same way.

"The world of football forgets you very, very fast when you're not playing," said the 31-year-old, who's back with the national team for the first time in two years.

"But when someone of Craig Bellamy's stature, the head coach of Wales, is calling me every month, or once every two weeks, to make sure I'm doing well... it's a massive, massive plus.

"Rather than feeling a million miles away, it always made me feel I was in touching distance of getting back in."

You can understand why Burns initially feared the worst.

He was out for almost a year after suffering a torn anterior cruciate ligament during Ipswich Town's defeat at Liverpool in January 2025.

By the time he returned, 11 months later, Ipswich were back in the Championship, and Burns was off Wales' radar as they prepared for their ultimately unsuccessful bid to reach the 2026 World Cup via the play-offs.

The Cardiff-born winger was never completely off Bellamy's mind, though, and now he wants to make up for lost international minutes by playing a part in the Nations League campaign that began with Thursday's 1-0 defeat in Portugal.

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC One Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

'You're only one second away from disaster'

Burns did not make it off the subs' bench in Lisbon, but hopes to get some minutes in Wales' second Nations League tie against Denmark in Copenhagen on Sunday, 27 October.

After the injury trauma that cut short his fairytale journey from League One to the Premier League with Ipswich, though, he is just pleased to be back on the international scene at all.

"You just have to remember you're only one second away from disaster, really," said Burns.

"That's how I felt when the injury happened. You feel that could be the end of your career because you never know how bad the injury is initially.

"And when you've had surgery, and your knee's like a balloon, you're thinking 'how on earth am I even going to walk again, never mind play'.

"Everything heals in time, though, and it was just about making sure I got the rehab right. The phone calls from Craig, knowing he had a similar injury when he was younger as a player, meant so much to me."

Burns could have been playing Premier League football again this season, having helped Ipswich bounce straight back to the top flight in the 2025-26 campaign.

But the former Fleetwood winger chose instead to drop two divisions to join Leicester City, who have struggled to adapt to life in League One under former Swansea City boss Russell Martin.

"I could've done another year at Ipswich, and I was weighing up whether to finish the story of playing a full season in the Premier League (which injury deprived him of the previous time) - a level I'd worked so hard to get back to," said Burns.

"But I also had to think about the longevity of my career, and in the end I took the option of a longer contract at Leicester and possibly recreating what I'd already done at Ipswich (back-to-back promotions)."

Such a journey might seem remote right now, with Leicester sitting 13th in League One with just two wins from their opening seven games, but Burns insists the Foxes will improve as the season goes on.

"We all know the story - Leicester, Premier League champions 10 years ago, amazing Champions League run, FA Cup winners and now sort of sitting mid-table in League One," he said.

"But it feels like they're very much in the same spot as when I went into Ipswich.

"It's a chance to recreate something that I've done in the past with an amazing manager (Martin) who obviously gets a lot of stick.

"He has a style of play and a philosophy that's very, very football-based and high risk but when that works it's amazing.

"Trust me - I've played against very good Russell Martin teams and they're very hard to play against, but it's a process and processes take a long time.

"I've got no doubt it's going to pick up, for sure."

From League One to Haaland on the horizon

Burns' last outing for Leicester was a 30-minute cameo off the bench at Barnsley on 19 September.

One week on, he hopes to step back onto the international stage for the first time since starting Wales' 1-0 win over Montenegro in Nations League B in October 2024.

From Oakwell in Barnsley to Copenhagen in Denmark, followed by a Cardiff City Stadium meeting with Erling Haaland's Norway on Thursday, 1 October.

"Going from the weekly level of football I'm now at to possibly playing against Norway, Denmark or Portugal (at home next month)... obviously the gap in quality is going to be massive," said Burns.

"But I've had experience of playing in the Premier League and against very good international teams.

"The one that stands out for me is when we played Netherlands away in the Nations League (in 2022), and I was on the same pitch as (midfielder) Frenkie de Jong - still to this day the best player I've ever played against or witnessed on a football field.

"So just drawing on experiences like that, and big games I've played in, will definitely help if I do get on the pitch against Denmark and Norway.

"It's just so exciting to be involved in games like these."

articles.title: Jose Mourinho at Real Madrid: What needs to improve after mixed start?
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho only returned to Real Madrid in July but a lot needs to improve in order for there to be a title race in La Liga.
articles.body:
When Jose Mourinho walked back through the doors at Real Madrid this summer, 13 years had passed since he last left the club.

He returned with a familiar reputation and enormous expectations, but facing a very different challenge.

Mourinho was handed a three-year contract, with the club hoping he could restore stability as well as success after two trophyless seasons.

Now, seven league matches into his second spell, some of the familiar tensions of last season have already resurfaced.

Defeat by rivals Atletico Madrid has left supporters questioning Real Madrid's consistency and Mourinho's approach.

The Portuguese coach now has plenty of time to consider his options during an unusually long three-week international break. Madrid do not play again until they host Villarreal on Saturday, 10 October - and travel to Barcelona two weeks later.

Mourinho has concerns about the break, but it is an early opportunity to take stock and prepare for a run of fixtures that could tell us much more about the direction of his second spell at the Bernabeu.

Mourinho prints out 'red card' incidents after Real lose derby

An iron fist joining a broken team: Inside Mourinho's Real return

For Mourinho, the derby defeat at Atletico Madrid was a sobering reminder of the scale of the challenge he has taken on.

Despite blaming much of the loss on two first-half decisions he felt went against his side - Cristian Romero escaping a red card for his studs-up challenge on Jude Bellingham and Lee Kang-in going unpunished for a similar challenge on Federico Valverde - the reality is that their performance was simply not good enough.

It means Real Madrid sit fourth in La Liga, with defending champions Barcelona already six points ahead. They have won all seven of their league games, scoring 31 goals, with Raphinha already scoring 12 times.

Atletico sit second and Real Betis third, both five points behind Hansi Flick's side.

The only time Real Madrid have overturned a six-point deficit to Barcelona at the top of La Liga was in Fabio Capello's 2006-07 title triumph.

A clear issue from the defeat at Atletico was Madrid's lack of control in midfield.

Mourinho started Aurelien Tchouameni alongside Valverde, with Bellingham playing further forward. The pairing gave Madrid energy and defensive security, but they struggled to control the tempo or create enough from deeper areas. Bernardo Silva was introduced for the final eight minutes, but by then Madrid were already chasing the game.

That presents Mourinho with an interesting selection decision. Against opponents who defend in a compact shape, Madrid may need more creativity and control from midfield.

Silva's ability to dictate the rhythm of a game makes him an obvious option, while Arda Guler offers another creative presence further forward.

Mourinho doesn't necessarily need to abandon the double pivot, but he does need to find a way for Real to have more control of matches.

There is no shortage of individual attacking quality at Real Madrid. The problem is making it work consistently as a unit.

Against Atletico, Madrid struggled to create clear chances. Kylian Mbappe was largely ineffective and hardly touched the ball, while Vinicius Jr was substituted shortly after Dean Huijsen's red card early in the second half.

Mourinho has three players, in Vinicius, Mbappe and Bellingham, capable of deciding matches on their own.

Bellingham's ability to carry the ball forward, arrive late in the box and link midfield with attack is another important part of Madrid's attacking threat, but Mourinho needs to ensure the trio complement rather than crowd each other.

Vinicius needs to rediscover the explosiveness and directness that makes him so difficult to defend, while Mbappe needs a greater supply of chances rather than being asked to create opportunities for himself.

There is another attacking option Mourinho could turn to more often.

Carlos Espi has already made an impression since joining the club, scoring the 90th-minute winner against Espanyol on his league debut before doing it again in stoppage time against Elche.

The 21-year-old has therefore shown he can make an impact when given game time.

With Madrid still working out how best to balance Vinicius, Mbappe and Bellingham, Espi offers Mourinho another option - particularly when Madrid need a focal point in the final stages of matches.

His early impact suggests he deserves more opportunities to show what he can do.

The other major concern is what happens when Madrid lose the ball.

Atletico repeatedly found space around Madrid's midfield and were able to attack quickly, while Huijsen's red card made the situation even more difficult. If Mourinho wants his side to press aggressively and commit numbers forward, Tchouameni and Valverde must provide enough protection when possession is lost.

Against Atletico, Denzel Dumfries, Ibrahima Konate, Huijsen and Marc Cucurella lined up in front of Thibaut Courtois. There is quality in that back four, but Mourinho will want greater cohesion - particularly when Madrid's full-backs push forward.

Courtois' performance showed how important he remains, with the goalkeeper making several important saves to keep Madrid in the game. The aim for Mourinho will be to reduce those situations and make Madrid harder to expose when attacks break down.

The veteran Portuguese needs to come up with some new answers to his team's problems quickly, or there may not be much of a title race.

articles.title: El durísimo adiós de Sandra Alonso al Mundial horas antes de la gran cita: “Le embestí y poco más recuerdo…”
articles.standfirst: La española no podrá disputar la prueba élite tras sufrir un accidente en el último entrenamiento: “Fisura del húmero, varias abrasiones y maquillaje de asfalto canadiense”
articles.summary: La española no podrá disputar la prueba élite tras sufrir un accidente en el último entrenamiento: “Fisura del húmero, varias abrasiones y maquillaje de asfalto canadiense”
articles.body: Sandra Alonso no tomará la salida en la prueba élite femenina del Mundial de Montreal. La ciclista española sufrió un duro accidente durante el último entrenamiento, apenas un día antes de una de las carreras más importantes de la temporada, y tendrá que regresar a casa con una fisura en el húmero, numerosas abrasiones y el lógico disgusto de perderse la cita mundialista. La propia corredora explicó horas después cómo se produjo el percance. “Esta noche escribo este post un poco triste. Esta mañana entrenando, el día previo a la carrera más importante del año, un ciclista al que adelantaba se le ocurrió darse la vuelta sin mirar atrás. Le embestí y poco más recuerdo…”, cuenta Alonso. El golpe fue lo suficientemente fuerte como para obligarla a pasar por el hospital y confirmar lo que ya se temía dentro de la selección española. “Por lo tanto, mañana el número 22 no saldrá”, anunció la valenciana. La noticia supone un importante contratiempo para España. Gema Pascual, seleccionadora nacional, había destacado precisamente el gran momento en el que llegaba Sandra y la importancia que debía tener dentro del plan colectivo. “Venía en un gran momento de forma, con muchas ganas y mucha ilusión. Todos teníamos mucha confianza en Sandra y creo que iba a hacer un grandísimo trabajo. Era primordial para nuestras corredoras y para la selección”, reconoció en Radio MARCA. Pascual conoció el accidente prácticamente en plena competición. “Justo antes de la carrera júnior nos llamaron para decirnos que se había accidentado y tuvieron que llevarla al hospital. Tiene, parece, una fisura en el húmero y un buen golpe en la cara”, relataba. Dentro del susto, la seleccionadora puso el foco en que las consecuencias no fueran todavía mayores. “Damos gracias de que, dentro de lo que cabe, sea chapa y pintura y tengamos a Sandra bien, que es lo más importante”. Sandra, pese a la decepción, quiso lanzar inmediatamente un mensaje de ánimo a sus compañeras. “Sí saldrá una de las mejores selecciones que ha tenido España en los últimos años. Así que a demostrar lo que valéis y a disfrutar del sufrimiento”, escribió mencionando a Sara Martín, Mireia Benito, Mavi García, Usoa Ostolaza y Paula Blasi. La ciclista tampoco quiso que su accidente empañara el extraordinario Mundial que está protagonizando España en Montreal. “Nada que penar y que quite la alegría de toda una nación por la lluvia de medallas que se están coleccionando”, añadió. España pierde así una pieza que estaba llamada a resultar fundamental para endurecer la prueba y proteger las principales bazas del equipo. Pascual había diseñado una carrera colectiva alrededor principalmente de Mavi García y Paula Blasi, pero el papel de Alonso estaba marcado en rojo por su capacidad para trabajar y seleccionar el grupo en un recorrido muy exigente. La selección ya enseñó su filosofía de carrera con las júniors. “Desde el primer momento salimos a destrozar la carrera. Necesitábamos moverla para que fueran cayendo corredoras”, explicó Pascual después del título mundial conquistado por Alejandra Neira. Para la élite, la mentalidad tampoco cambia pese a perder a Sandra: “Hay que ir a por todo”. Alonso, mientras tanto, ya piensa únicamente en recuperarse. “Por mi parte: fisura del húmero, varias abrasiones y maquillaje de asfalto canadiense. Toca volver a casa, descansar y recuperar”, cerró con optimismo. Horas antes del accidente que terminó apartándola del Mundial, Sandra Alonso había hablado con MARCA en Montreal sobre una temporada que definía como “una locura” por todo lo que había tenido que improvisar. “No tenía planeado nada más que dejarme llevar y correr todo lo que pudiera”, explicaba. Después de empezar con el gravel en febrero, aprovechar cada llamada de la selección y todas las oportunidades que encontró, hacía balance con orgullo: “Puedo estar muy contenta y muy satisfecha de todo el trabajo y de los resultados que han salido”. Su regreso al máximo nivel tampoco había sido sencillo. Alonso reconocía haber vivido meses de incertidumbre, especialmente pensando en su futuro. “Había momentos de frustración por pensar qué iba a pasar el año que viene. Me di este año de margen para intentar volver, pero pasaban los meses y todavía no veía nada claro para 2027”. La llamada del Laboral Kutxa cambió ese escenario y le permitió respirar después de haber llamado a numerosas puertas sin obtener respuesta. “He tenido que ir yo sola por mi cuenta, con ayuda de pequeños patrocinadores, gente de mi entorno y amigos que me han echado un cable, incluso económicamente para poder desplazarme a las competiciones”. Los resultados terminaron siendo su mejor argumento. “Creo que han hecho que la gente vea: ‘Sandra vuelve a ser Sandra, incluso una Sandra mejor’”, aseguraba. Y precisamente ahí situaba su gran ambición para la próxima temporada. “El reto es mejorar mi último año completo, que fue 2024. Ahora tengo más motivación y he descubierto que puedo ser incluso mejor que antes. Creo que 2027 puede ser un año muy bonito. Quiero volver a estar ahí, pelear, ganar carreras y que se vuelva a tener mi nombre en cuenta”. En esa reconstrucción deportiva también ocupa un lugar esencial su maternidad. Sandra reivindicaba que ser madre no le había impedido recuperar su mejor nivel: “Se puede, claro que se puede. Yo lo he demostrado y lo he vivido en mis propias carnes”. Su vida, decía, sigue girando alrededor de entrenar y cuidarse, aunque ahora disfruta “mucho más con la niña”. Y dejaba además una reflexión sobre la protección de las ciclistas que deciden formar una familia: “Más que una ley, tiene que salir de dentro. Tenemos que pensar en las mujeres, en sus vidas y en que puedan crear una familia igual que pueden hacerlo los hombres durante su carrera deportiva. Es más una cuestión humana que de ley”.

articles.title: Women's Super League: Analysis of Man Utd's tactics under new boss Eva Olid
articles.summary: Eva Olid promised high-possession attacking football at Manchester United, so why has it not worked yet?
articles.body:
Eva Olid was given the Manchester United job with a reputation for playing high-possession attacking football and her impressive spell at Hearts demonstrated those ideals.

In her opening weeks in the Women's Super League, however, she has struggled to get her team playing this type of dominant football, even if an eye-catching 10-1 win at Sheffield United in the League Cup on Wednesday suggested she was making progress.

On the WSL's opening night, United lost 2-1 to London City Lionesses before suffering a 5-0 defeat by Chelsea. They responded by drawing 1-1 with Arsenal in a performance far more pragmatic than many might have expected.

Following the turbulent start, we analysed Olid's United, unpacking her tactical approach and the tweaks she has made from predecessor Marc Skinner.

Man Utd put 10 past Blades as Olid gets first win

Olid's Man Utd take big step forward after 'intense week'

The differences between Skinner and Olid

Under Olid, United look to play out from the back. For a team ultimately wanting to dominate the ball, short passes help reduce the 50-50 nature of long balls.

Their build-up normally starts from a 4-2 or 3-2 base, with the central midfielders forming a narrow two.

The winger on the same side as the ball tends to stay high and wide, while the far-side winger drops deeper, playing alongside the number 10 and creating a box in midfield.

Although Skinner's United also used a 4-2 or 3-2 base, their principles were different.

His formation was generally a more stretched and symmetrical 3-2-2-3 with players given more fixed positions to occupy.

His number 10s were often asked to stay high in pockets, to either receive the ball in dangerous areas or drag opponents away to create space elsewhere.

Her central players are given greater licence to come towards the ball, likely to create overloads in the middle of the pitch.

For example, if Park switches from the flank into central midfield, should the opposition full-back follow her? If they do not, it should hand United a numerical advantage around the ball.

This reflects in where United now focus their play.

That is because when opponents defend zonally, crowding central areas gives United more numbers in the middle. If defences compensate by narrowing, space appears on the outside for unmarked players.

By comparison, Skinner placed fewer players centrally. As a result, possession was funnelled towards the flanks, where full-back, midfielder and winger combined in triangles.

As with all systems, there are trade-offs.

Skinner's more fixed structure could make it easier for brave opponents to match them player-for-player. In that situation, Olid's team would respond by moving another player towards the ball to create an overload.

Alternatively, by focusing on small-space combinations through the centre, Olid's United are more likely to lose possession in dangerous areas, making them more susceptible to counter-attacks, something that has been evident already in her tenure.

After three league games, United have averaged 37% possession, with Olid identifying two problems last weekend: "We lose simple passes and we cannot recognise the free player."

Goalkeeper Phallon Tullis-Joyce has struggled with the ball at her feet, lacking some of the qualities this system asks for. Chelsea's man-to-man pressure exposed that and prevented United from establishing prolonged possession.

She is not the only one making a tough adjustment to this more intricate approach.

Olid's tactics are designed to create numerical advantages to put players in space but United have not always found them even when the movement has been good.

Her style requires players to be better technically and quicker cognitively.

Playing through crowded central areas means receiving the ball under pressure, combining in small spaces and identifying the spare player. Those actions rely on chemistry and game understanding rather than simply following a pre-planned pattern.

Hinata Miyazawa and Julia Zigiotti-Olme have looked the best suited but developing the collective understanding and removing hesitation will take time.

For Chelsea's fourth goal, these trade-offs were seen clearly as United lost possession trying to play through the middle from deep and were punished in transition.

The tactical tweaks Olid has implemented

To her credit, Olid has adapted her approach.

There is recent evidence of Tullis-Joyce going long more often and against Arsenal, recalled Awujo provided a more capable target for those passes than Ella Toone.

This also allowed striker Elisabeth Terland to stay higher up the pitch rather than constantly dropping deep to engage in aerial duels or hold-up play.

She has also explained her approach when out of possession, telling Sky Sports: "We are a team who need to press high."

Against Chelsea, however, that press was repeatedly exposed.

With Monica Jusu Bah starting on the left and Terland leading the press, the former moved inside as the ball travelled wide to try to engage Chelsea midfielder Keira Walsh.

That allowed Blues right-back Ellie Carpenter freedom to advance, while on the other side Wieke Kaptein pinned back United left-back Andrea Medina.

In the second half, Olid adjusted. Terland became more passive alongside Toone, with the pair screening Chelsea's central midfielders.

That allowed Jusu Bah to stay wider and prevent easy access to Carpenter.

In the big win against Sheffield United on Wednesday, Manchester United's third and fourth goal came from an intense and co-ordinated press that forced the opposition to turn over the ball close to their own goal.

Implementing a new style takes time, particularly when players are being asked to use space and accept risk in ways they are not accustomed to.

A common problem for coaches with an ambitious game model is becoming too attached to the final version of it and ignoring what the current squad needs.

Olid does not appear to be falling into that trap.

"The focus [against Arsenal] was the defensive shape," she said. "It's trying to get them more confidence."

Attacking football in this more fluid manner may be the final goal but Olid appears willing to build towards it in steps.

Early on in her managerial role at Hearts, she showed similar flexibility, which won her points, the trust of her players, and a platform from which to create exciting football.

"The [attack] will come," Olid has said. "But we need to keep this [defensive structure], then from there, little by little, be an attacking team, create chances, score more goals."

And the League Cup victory did give some indication it has, although Sheffield United are bottom of WSL 2 in the early weeks of the season.

What will be key is to see how they build on that momentum for this weekend's WSL match against West Ham on Sunday.

articles.title: El milagro de Ibai Gómez en el Zaragoza
articles.standfirst: El técnico vasco ha logrado cambiar la dinámica perdedora que arrastraba el equipo aragonés desde hace años
articles.summary: El técnico vasco ha logrado cambiar la dinámica perdedora que arrastraba el equipo aragonés desde hace años
articles.body: Ibai Gómez ha instalado en Zaragoza el estado de ilusión. Algo que parecía muy difícil tras años infames. Sólo cuatro meses después de que el club aragonés sufriera el capítulo más duro de su historia con el descenso a Primera RFEF, el técnico vasco ha conseguido borrar todo el pesimismo y dudas que arrastraba el equipo maño y contagiar su optimismo de que puede ser una gran temporada con final feliz. El exigido y esperado. Es cierto que el campeonato solo acaba de empezar, se han jugado cinco jornadas, pero este Zaragoza gusta y se gusta. No aburre como el del pasado y, sobre todo transmite sensaciones que se parecen a las del 2019-2020 cuando se peleó por el ascenso a Primera división antes de que la pandemia hiciera trizas todo. Ibai es una clara apuesta de Lalo Arantegui, quien vio en él el entrenador ideal para reconstruir un puzzle roto. Gómez llegó con una propuesta de juego diferente y atractiva pero al principio complicada de asimilar de forma rápida por los futbolistas. Pero lo ha conseguido pronto. El Real Zaragoza ya tiene una identidad que va de la mano del gusto de una afición que se ha hartado de ver aberraciones de partidos en los que a veces ni se disparaba a puerta. Ahora, el juego es alegre, los jugadores se divierten en el campo y la plantilla está mostrando un hambre que ha estado ausente en las últimas temporadas. Quizá, también la categoría ayuda a jugar de esta manera, ya que parece menos física y defensiva que la Segunda. Y eso se agradece. El Real Zaragoza ha encadenado cuatro victorias consecutivas que ha hecho que afición y equipo vuelvan a reconciliarse. Ibai lo sabía desde un principio. Si le daban a su gente, su gente iba a estar con ellos. Así de sencillo. Eran ellos los que tenían que dar el primer paso tras un pasado durísimo. Y lo han dado. Porque si hay una cosa clara es que los seguidores blanquillos son justos y fieles y con este equipo de Ibai sí se identifican. El escudo vuelve a estar bien defendido y representado. Y así, el objetivo común del ascenso estará más cerca. Ojalá no se tuerza nada. El zaragocismo ya se merece una gran alegría.

articles.title: England vs Spain: UEFA Nations League – Predictions, teams, head-to-head
articles.summary: World champions Spain meet heavyweights England in a rematch of the UEFA Euro 2024 final.
articles.body:
Who : England vs Spain What : UEFA Nations League 2026-27 , Group A3 match Where : Wembley Stadium, London, United Kingdom When: Saturday, September 26, at 7:45pm (18:45 GMT) How to follow : Al Jazeera Sport will bring you all the build-up and live updates from 15:45 GMT.

England begin their new Nations League campaign with a heavyweight home fixture against the reigning world champions, Spain.

Saturday’s clash at Wembley will be a rematch of the UEFA Euro 2024 final , which Spain won 2-1 in Berlin, Germany.

La Roja, the 2023 Nations League winners, are looking to add a second title to their collection, having also finished runners-up to Portugal in the last edition in 2025.

England, on the other hand, enjoyed their best result in the inaugural 2019 edition, finishing third. They return to League A this time after winning Group B2 in their previous appearance.

Competing in the top division of the structured competition, Croatia and Czechia are the other teams in Group A3 with England and Spain.

The UEFA Nations League was founded in 2018 to reduce the number of meaningless friendlies and give nations competitive matches against equally-ranked teams.

In this competition, countries from across Europe participate in a league structure, which features promotion and relegation.

Opta’s supercomputer has handed Spain a 40.2 percent probability of victory, while England have a 33.6 percent chance of winning. The odds of a draw stand at 26.2 percent.

Spain have won six of their last nine meetings with England.

England and Spain last met at the UEFA Euro 2024 final, in which goals from Nico Williams and Mikel Oyarzabal handed La Roja a 2-1 championship victory. That result marked a record-breaking fourth European crown for Spain.

Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham (England): All English hopes will once again rest on captain and Ballon d’Or frontrunner Harry Kane of Bayern Munich, who recently became the fastest player to 100 German Bundesliga goals. Elsewhere, attacking midfielder Jude Bellingham has made an impressive start under new Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho, producing three goals and three assists in seven La Liga appearances.

Ferran Torres and Lamine Yamal (Spain) : La Roja fans will be excited to see Ferran Torres in the national team colours this weekend after he scored a hat-trick in his first Champions League appearance for new club Paris Saint-Germain. His former Barcelona teammate Lamine Yamal, too, is enjoying a strong start this season, with his seven goals rated joint-second-highest in La Liga.

Thomas Tuchel, England coach : “I think the more you analyse Spain and their last matches they played in, you have to admire the way in which they defend. They added this to their game. It’s difficult for every single team in the world to create chances against Spain. But we have a plan, we have ambition, and we want to be the exception to the rule. At the moment, though, they are a very complete team.”

Luis de la Fuente, Spain coach: “I know what these players are made of. We are not satisfied with what we have done so far, I guarantee it. One story is over; now another begins. Another one in which we are very excited. We want to continue doing important things, to continue making records as historic as those that are being achieved.”

articles.title: Daniel Osvaldo, ingresado en la UCI tras una intervención urgente en el pulmón
articles.standfirst: El exdelantero del Espanyol permanece bajo vigilancia médica
articles.summary: El exdelantero del Espanyol permanece bajo vigilancia médica
articles.body: Preocupación por el estado de salud de Daniel Osvaldo. El exfutbolista argentino del Espanyol, entre otros equipos, permanece ingresado en la unidad de cuidados intensivos de un hospital de Llavallol, en la provincia de Buenos Aires. Osvaldo tuvo que ser operado de urgencia después de sufrir un grave derrame pleural en el pulmón derecho. Según las informaciones desde Argentina llevaba varios días encontrándose mal y fue su hermana quien lo trasladó al hospital al encontrarlo en un delicado estado. Tras la intervención, ha quedado bajo vigilancia médica y su pronóstico es reservado. Los últimos años de Osvaldo estuvieron marcados por importantes dificultades personales. En marzo de 2024, el exdelantero publicó un vídeo en sus redes sociales en el que reconoció que llevaba tiempo luchando contra una fuerte depresión y que había tenido problemas con el alcohol y las drogas. También explicó que estaba siguiendo un tratamiento psiquiátrico y que atravesaba una etapa de aislamiento y falta de autoestima. Aquella confesión llegó después de varios años alejados del fútbol profesional. Osvaldo había pasado de ser un jugador de élite a centrarse en la música y en una nueva vida fuera de los terrenos de juego, un cambio que, según sus propias palabras, también supuso un importante impacto personal y económico. Meses después, sin embargo, el propio Osvaldo explicó que había avanzado en su recuperación. En una entrevista publicada a finales de 2024 aseguró que continuaba en tratamiento y que se encontraba mucho mejor, afirmando que no había vuelto a sufrir una recaída.

articles.title: Un expresidente del Manchester City, "en shock" pero contundente: "La sanción debe ser algo más que económica"
articles.standfirst: David Bernstein estuvo al frente de la entidad entre 1998 y 2003 y ha valorado el caso
articles.summary: David Bernstein estuvo al frente de la entidad entre 1998 y 2003 y ha valorado el caso
articles.body: David Bernstein, expresidente del Manchester City entre 1998 y 2003, considera que una sanción económica no sería suficiente para castigar al club tras confirmarse la culpabilidad de 114 de las 115 acusaciones de irregularidades financieras. Bernstein reconoció en Times Radio que la noticia le dejó "en estado de shock". "Es normal, soy un seguidor del Manchester City y lo he sido durante 70 años", explicó el exdirigente, que lamentó que este proceso haya ensombrecido la etapa más exitosa de la historia reciente del club. "Ver todo esto empañado de esta manera es muy triste. Me siento especialmente mal por los maravillosos seguidores del club que han permanecido con él en las buenas y en las malas", afirmó en estas declaraciones recogidas por The Guardian. El antiguo presidente del City también reclamó que el proceso de apelación se resuelva cuanto antes. "Todo este proceso ya ha durado demasiado", señaló. "El proceso de apelación no puede prolongarse año tras año; creo que sería un desastre. No solo para este caso en particular, sino para el fútbol inglés en general", añadió. Sobre el castigo que debería recibir el club, Bernstein evitó concretar una sanción, pero sí dejó una reflexión contundente: "Si, tras la apelación, se confirma la culpabilidad, mi querido club se enfrentará a una sanción muy severa". Y añadió: "El dinero no es suficiente; lamentablemente, tendría que ser algo más drástico".

articles.title: Israel v Republic of Ireland: Republic of Ireland news conference delayed before Israel game
articles.summary: The Republic of Ireland delay the pre-match news conference planned for Sunday's Uefa Nations League game against Israel in Hungary - a fixture campaigners have called on them to boycott.
articles.body:
The Republic of Ireland have delayed the pre-match news conference planned for Sunday's Uefa Nations League game against Israel in Hungary - a fixture campaigners have called on them to boycott.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's team are scheduled to meet Israel in Debrecen at 19:45 BST, with the return fixture in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October.

They have faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace.

Former Republic of Ireland manager Brian Kerr and ex-international James McClean are among those to have backed calls for a boycott.

However, there are also Irish supporters, perhaps less vocal, who have always believed that the match should be played with supporters in attendance.

Following Thursday's 1-0 defeat by Kosovo, midfielder Jason Knight opined he didn't think "the game should be going ahead" , while winger Chiedozie Ogbene urged the public to not "put the pressure on us" regarding their approach to the scheduled game.

Hallgrimsson and a player were scheduled to meet the media at 09:15 BST (10.15 local time), before training, but the conference was delayed shortly beforehand.

A Uefa official entered the room to inform waiting media teams that the press conference was postponed until after training, which would have been about 11:30 BST (12.30 local time).

But shortly afterwards, the Uefa official returned to the media room to announce that the Republic of Ireland's training session had also been postponed, with no time given for when it might take place. There is also no confirmed time for the news conference.

The fixture has been embroiled in controversy since the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

A team meeting took place on Friday for players to air their views on Sunday's game and the return fixture in Serbia.

The players were expected to release a statement at Saturday's news conference, but the delay has added further uncertainty, with some reports of at least one player wishing to withdraw from the squad.

It has since emerged the news conference, scheduled to take place at the stadium, is now set to be staged at the team hotel, with Uefa unable to provide information regarding the delay.

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

articles.title: Militao pasa la última prueba y ya solo queda la puesta a punto
articles.standfirst: El central ha recibido la visita del médico que le operó de su grave lesión del tendón el pasado mes de abril y ha dado vía libre a su regreso
articles.summary: El central ha recibido la
articles.body: El Real Madrid espera a una de sus grandez bazas en defensa. Y no es otro que Eder Militao, que pasa hace ya tiempo un auténtico calvario con las lesiones. El central tiene buenas noticias después de haber recibido la visita en Valdebebas del médico que le operó, el finlandés Lasse Lampainen. "Gran día en Madrid con @edermilitao y el personal médico y de rendimiento de @realmadrid. Un día completo dedicado al regreso mientras Éder continúa progresando de acuerdo al plan tras la cirugía por su lesión grave de tendón. Fue un placer para nosotros aportar nuestra experiencia y experiencia en su proceso de vuelta a los terrenos de juego, con el objetivo final de ayudarlo a regresar a salvo y actuar de nuevo al más alto nivel. Muchas gracias a Éder y a todo el staff del Real Madrid por la excelente colaboración y un día muy exitoso. Volver al campo es un hito. Volver a tu nivel más alto de rendimiento es el objetivo", comenta el doctor finlandés en sus redes. Militao fue operado de una rotura del tendón proximal del bíceps femoral el 28 de abril de 2026 y el tiempo de baja estipulado era de cinco meses, por lo que el jugador está ya en la recta final. Hace apenas unos días, el central se dejó ver en el campo en una exigente sesión física en la que mostraba ya su buena recuperación. Con esta test del doctor que le operó y que ha resultado muy positivo, ya solo queda empezar a trabajar con el grupo y ser uno más. Su regreso dependería ya de cómo vaya evolucionando con el trabajo con el resto de compañeros y el tiempo que necesite para alcanzar la mejor forma para volver al equipo, pero debería ser este mes de octubre. Militao tiene por delante un desafío mayúsculo, volver a jugar y alcanzar el nivel que le hizo para casi todo el mundo ser uno de los mejores del mundo en su puesto después de ya cerca de 800 días de baja entre las tres últimas temporadas. La pesadilla empezó en la temporada 23-24 con la rotura del ligamento cruzado anterior de la rodilla izquierda. Fueron 231 días de baja. La siguiente temporada, tres lesiones más, entre ellas una nueva rotura completa del ligamento cruzado anterior con afectación de ambos meniscos, esta vez de la pierna derecha. Otros 255 días fuera de los terrenos de juego. Y la pasada temporada sufrió otras cuatro lesiones que se traducen en total desde 2023 en 781 días de baja.

articles.title: Manchester City charges: Legal fight could spiral out of control, says former executive
articles.summary: Manchester City's legal fight with the Premier League has the potential to "spiral out of control" a former top club executive has warned.
articles.body:
Manchester City 's legal fight with the Premier League has the potential to "spiral out of control", a former top club executive has warned.

Christian Purslow, a former Liverpool managing director and Aston Villa chief executive, who also held a senior role at Chelsea , said the case could begin a chain of events that would be "appalling for the game".

City have been found guilty of the vast majority of 115 charges brought forward by the Premier League.

The club were accused of a wide range of rule breaches which centred around claims that they inflated sponsorship revenue from connected companies and made other "off the books" payments to circumvent football's financial rules.

Premier League clubs are seeking legal advice about compensation relating to the charges, while BBC Sport has been told that City will appeal.

Sanctions on the club are yet to be announced, but repercussions could include a points deduction, expulsion from the Premier League or a huge fine.

Speaking on Radio 4's Today programme, Purslow appeared alongside football law expert Paul Gilroy KC, who described the case as a "seismic moment for world football".

Purslow said: "It's a sort of 'where does this end?' because if you look at every single season - the nine seasons which we now know Manchester City breached rules - then all of their 19 Premier League rivals in that season, to differing extents, suffered easy-to-compute loss. Whether it was a place in the Premier League - every place was worth £3m.

"Teams that came fifth who didn't make the Champions League maybe lost tens of millions of pounds - and of course teams that were relegated. Let's say the team that finished 18th would've finished 17th if Manchester City weren't there. And they, of course, suffered huge loss.

"If you add all those claims up, over nine years, and that's just in the Premier League, you can see that the potential here for this to spiral out of control is huge.

"I really hope that common sense prevails here and that there is a comprehensive solution between the authorities and Manchester City that looks at all these issues and tries to draw a line in the sand.

"Because a never-ending waterfall of legal claims and uncertainties for another four or five years would be absolutely appalling for the game."

Gilroy added that, so far, four clubs have put in protective claims "reserving the right to claim compensation if City are found guilty".

Man City and the 115 charges - key questions answered

Man City fans face up to reality of guilty verdict

Everton told to pay Burnley £35m over PSR breach

The news, broken by the Athletic, , external came 1,327 days after City were charged by the Premier League in February 2023 following a four-year investigation, and 22 months after a hearing by an independent commission concluded.

No official announcement has been made by the Premier League, which has declined to comment.

Manchester City declined to comment on whether they had been found guilty, instead providing a statement which read: "Premier League process remains ongoing with significant elements to be completed, and subject to strict confidentiality.

"The club has diligently respected due process for eight years on the basis that the Premier League board and executive would behave as an independent, impartial and fair-minded regulator, free from partisan influence."

Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy has urged the Premier League to come to a quick resolution.

She told BBC Radio 5 Live: "I think most football fans will be feeling that this is not a good moment for football as a whole and I think Manchester City fans will be feeling very, very anxious about what happens next.

"It's very unsettling for football fans and I hope that it can be resolved as swiftly as possible.

"I will obviously look very closely as what comes out of this but we can't apply those rules for the Premier League. They have got to do it themselves and are going to have to resolve this as swiftly as possible - not just for the sake of Manchester City but for the sake of football."

Former chairman Bernstein feels 'absolutely awful'

City won eight trophies in the period covered by the case, including three Premier League titles, three EFL Cups, one Community Shield and one FA Cup.

The charges cover the managerial tenures of Roberto Mancini and Manuel Pellegrini, and the first two years under Pep Guardiola, who left the club at the end of last season after 10 years in charge.

Former Manchester City chairman David Bernstein told Times Radio he felt "absolutely awful" on hearing the news of City being found guilty - but admitted any punishment would have to be "more drastic" than a fine.

"To see all this tarnished in this way is very sad," he said.

"I feel particularly bad for the wonderful supporters of the club who've stayed with the club through thick and thin.

"This whole process has taken too long already. So the appeal process now has to be done quickly because you've got the club playing with this cloud over its head and it's just not viable.

"The appeal process cannot go on for year after year, I think that would be a disaster, not just for this particular case but for English football generally. The timing is crucial."

He continued: "I can't give a view on the punishment. If they are found, after the appeal, guilty of 115 charges, my beloved club is going to face a very severe penalty.

"All I would say is that money is not sufficient, it would have to be something, unfortunately, more drastic than that."

Meanwhile, singer-songwriter Noel Gallagher says he is "shocked" at the news and it is "quite sad" for players and fans.

"A little surprised when I heard it on the radio. Surprised because the club have assured us all along that they vehemently denied any of these charges," the Oasis star and City fan said on the Let Me Talk podcast.

"So it was a bit of a shock to find out that we've been found guilty of all but one. But really overall just quite sad really. Sad for the fans and for the players."

articles.title: Karim Adeyemi talks Barcelona move, Flick, Gordon competition: ‘Honoured to be at this club’
articles.summary: When Karim Adeyemi joined Barcelona for a deal worth €22 million, it seemed like quite the bargain for the Blaugrana.One month into the new season, Adeyemi h...
articles.body:
When Karim Adeyemi joined Barcelona for a deal worth €22 million, it seemed like quite the bargain for the Blaugrana .

One month into the new season, Adeyemi has certainly proved himself more than a bargain , with the forward racking up six goal involvements in eight matches, scoring a few bangers in the process.

Currently part of the German national team fold under Jurgen Klopp, Adeyemi recently sat down with AS , where he talked about life in Barcelona, competition with other attackers in the team, as well as Hansi Flick, among other things.

The German admitted that while he feels good, his adaptation is still very much a work in progress.

" I think it's hard to say. I feel really, really good, but as for everything being settled, I don't think we're at that point yet. I'm not completely here yet. Now I have to learn the language, which is important to me," he said.

Adeyemi missed a big chance against the Netherlands. (Photo by Dean Mouhtaropoulos/Getty Images)

"It's hard to be 100% settled in just a month or two, but I feel really good and I can't wait to be here much longer," he added.

The forward revealed how he has been spending his downtime, painting a picture of a quiet, family-oriented life by the sea.

"I went to the beach, to the sea, I went swimming. I think it was the most enjoyable thing for me. I still do it from time to time," he stated.

"I like being at home with my family around me. I only go out occasionally. But I like being at home and going to the beach; that's my peace and what I need for my life."

Adeyemi, who clocked a remarkable 36 km/h against Levante, was asked about the secret of his pace and whether or not he had any athletics background before.

"No, never (laughs). I never did athletics. When I was younger, I used to do a lot of backflips and things like that on the trampoline. Beyond that, I'm good at sports in general, but I've always only ever played football," he said.

The winger also described his instinctive approach to the game.

"Yes, I'd even say it's pure instinct. My best games are when I'm not thinking about anything on the pitch and the movements just come naturally. I try to create things and hope they work out. I'm happy to play with such great teammates."

Adeyemi is back in Germany fold under new coach Jurgen Klopp. (Photo by Lars Baron/Getty Images)

Adeyemi, who knows Flick from their time in Germany, was happy with his start but insisted he can offer more.

"I believe I can always give more. But I'm happy for every minute I play, every goal I score, and every victory we achieve. If I can help the team, even better. We want to win everything," he said.

"If he's happy, I'm happy (laughs). I hope he is. I've had a good start, but I always work every day to improve, to contribute more to the team," he said when asked about his relationship with Flick.

He also expressed his gratitude for the warm welcome from supporters.

"I have a job here, and I'm truly happy and honoured to be at this club. I'm not a guy who tries to fake a show; I do my thing, I'm authentic, and I'm always honest. The fans' love is incredible."

Finally, Adeyemi addressed his competition with fellow summer signing Anthony Gordon , viewing it as a positive for the team.

"I think the best thing is for all the players to believe they can be starters. We have to compete because football is about competition, but we also have to maintain the good atmosphere in the locker room. That's the most important thing," he concluded.

Both Adeyemi and Gordon have integrated well into the team, offering different qualities that have cumulatively made Barcelona a much more complete attacking side.

articles.summary: Los detalles del estreno de la segunda estrella de España
articles.body: La selección española afronta un apasionante duelo de alto voltaje en la UEFA Nations League rindiendo visita a Inglaterra en Wembley. Tras coronarse campeona del mundo, la plantilla dirigida por Luis de la Fuente recupera para este compromiso todo el potencial en sus bandas gracias al regreso al cien por cien de Lamine Yamal, Nico Williams, Yeremy Pino y Víctor Muñoz, quienes superaron los problemas físicos que condicionaron su participación en la cita mundialista. Con la solidez de un bloque que ha demostrado saber competir y ganar ante cualquier adversidad, la Roja busca dar un golpe de autoridad a domicilio para afianzar sus opciones en el torneo continental. Por su parte, la Inglaterra de Thomas Tuchel encara este enfrentamiento mermada por una plaga de bajas de última hora. El técnico alemán no podrá contar con futbolistas capitales como Declan Rice, Cole Palmer, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo y Tino Livramento, lo que le ha obligado a reestructurar la lista y citar de urgencia a James Garner y Morgan Gibbs-White. Pese a estas ausencias de peso, los 'Three Lions' confían en el liderazgo de figuras como Jude Bellingham, Trent Alexander-Arnold o Harry Kane para hacerse fuertes en casa y tomarse la revancha deportiva ante el conjunto español. El partido entre Inglaterra y España, correspondiente a la UEFA Nations League, se disputará este sábado 26 de septiembre a las 20:45 horas (horario peninsular español). El encuentro entre la selección inglesa y el combinado español se podrá ver en directo por televisión e internet en España de forma gratuita a través de La 1 de TVE y en la plataforma RTVE Play. Sigue toda la actualidad de la UEFA Nations League, el minuto a minuto del encuentro y la última hora de la selección española en MARCA.com y escucha la retransmisión en directo en Radio MARCA.

articles.title: Republic of Ireland news conference delayed before controversial Israel game
articles.summary: The Republic of Ireland delay the pre-match news conference planned for Sunday's Uefa Nations League game against Israel in Hungary - a fixture campaigners h...
articles.body:
The Republic of Ireland have delayed the pre-match news conference planned for Sunday's Uefa Nations League game against Israel in Hungary - a fixture campaigners have called on them to boycott.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's team are scheduled to meet Israel in Debrecen at 19:45 BST, with the return fixture in Backa Topola, Serbia on 4 October.

They have faced calls to withdraw from the games because of the ongoing Israel-Gaza war with a "Stop The Game" campaign - organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine - gathering pace.

Former Republic of Ireland manager Brian Kerr and ex-international James McClean are among those to have backed calls for a boycott.

However, there are also Irish supporters, perhaps less vocal, who have always believed that the match should be played with supporters in attendance.

Following Thursday's 1-0 defeat by Kosovo, midfielder Jason Knight opined he didn't think "the game should be going ahead" , while winger Chiedozie Ogbene urged the public to not "put the pressure on us" regarding their approach to the scheduled game.

Hallgrimsson and a player were scheduled to meet the media at 09:15 BST (10.15 local time), before training, but the conference was delayed shortly beforehand.

A Uefa official entered the room to inform waiting media teams that the press conference was postponed until after training, which would have been about 11:30 BST (12.30 local time).

But shortly afterwards, the Uefa official returned to the media room to announce that the Republic of Ireland's training session had also been postponed, with no time given for when it might take place. There is also no confirmed time for the news conference.

The fixture has been embroiled in controversy since the two teams were drawn to play each other in Group B3.

A team meeting took place on Friday for players to air their views on Sunday's game and the return fixture in Serbia.

The players were expected to release a statement at Saturday's news conference, but the delay has added further uncertainty, with some reports of at least one player wishing to withdraw from the squad.

It has since emerged the news conference, scheduled to take place at the stadium, is now set to be staged at the team hotel, with Uefa unable to provide information regarding the delay.

The armed Palestinian group Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023, killing about 1,200 people and taking 251 hostages.

In response, Israel launched a massive military offensive in Gaza, during which more than 73,000 people have been killed, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the United Nations.

articles.title: Flick verá en directo el Inglaterra - España: un tercio de la plantilla del Barça, en Wembley
articles.standfirst: Tiene previsto estar hoy en las gradas del mítico estadio: el equipo está de vacaciones
articles.summary: Un tercio de la plantilla culé está hoy en Wembley
articles.body: Hansi Flick dio vacaciones a sus jugadores desde ayer viernes, hicieron trabajo en el gimnasio de la Ciudad Deportiva, hasta el lunes 5 de octubre. Pero él no descansa. Tiene previsto ver en directo el encuentro de mañana entre Inglaterra y España. Tiene a ¡8! jugadores citados para este compromiso internacional. Un tercio de su plantilla. El combinado de de Tuchel recibe hoy a La Roja, a las 20:45 horas en Wembley. El partido corresponde a la jornada 1 de la fase de grupos de la UEFA Nations League. Y Flick estará en las gradas del mítico estadio inglés. El técnico quiere disfrutar de un gran encuentro, pero, además, tiene a una tercera parte de su plantilla en ese compromiso, y desea ver a sus hombres en directo. Con el bloque de Luis de la Fuente hay siete futbolistas azulgranas, Cubarsí, Eric, Rodri, Pedri, Fermín, Olmo y Lamine; y con Inglaterra está Anthony Gordon. Hoy también tiene partido Livakovic: Croacia se mide a Chequia también a las 20:45 horas. El Barcelona está orgulloso de sus internacionales, pero existe también cierta preocupación por el riesgo de lesiones. El equipo catalán tiene a 17 jugadores citados con sus respectivas selecciones. Además de los españoles que están con la absoluta y Xavi Espart y Marc Bernal, que están con la absoluta, están citados: Gordon, con Inglaterra; Adeyemi, con Alemania; Raphinha, con Brasil; Cancelo, con Portugal; Koundé, con Francia; Livakovic, con Croacia; Abdelkarim, con Egipto; y Bisiwu, con la sub 21 de Bélgica. Raphinha preocupa especialmente, ya que no sólo es su jugador más en forma y se ha lesionado en anteriores convocatorias sino que, además, tiene un largo desplazamiento: ha viajado Australia, donde Brasil juega dos encuentros, y luego se trasladará a la India. En el primero de los compromisos, el atacante azulgrana completó los 90 minutos. No está siendo el único. La mayoría de los internacionales culés están teniendo protagonismo con sus combinados. Koundé intervino en los 90 minutos en la victoria de Francia contra Turquía (0-1); Marc Bernal también salió de inicio con la sub 21, en la derrota (2-1) en el cruce frente a Finlandia y no fue sustituido, sí que fue relevado, en cambio, Xavi Espart, que sólo jugó la primera mitad; Cancelo fue cambiado en el 90' del partido entre Portugal y Gales (1-0); Adeyemi estuvo 80' sobre el césped en el compromiso de Alemania contra Países Bajos (1-1); Hamza Abdelkarim participó 28' con Egipto en el empate con Angola (0-0)...
